crop.notes: The 'At Tom Allen's.' section is complete. It is one section of the larger 'Closed at Midnight' article about saloons obeying the Sunday closing law; the headline and the rest of the article are on the page but not in the clipping.

ocr.notes: Drops 'and the crowd lingered' after 'the officer had disappeared'; otherwise accurate.

title.suggested: Allen's saloon closes at midnight under the Sunday law

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that on the first night saloons had to close at midnight for Sunday, the largest crowd was at Tom Allen's, which threw out a drunk and closed its doors at 12:40.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Sunday, May 20, 1888, page 7. The section sits within 'Closed at Midnight. Saloon-keepers observe the Sunday law all over the city.'

facts.fact: When St. Louis saloons were made to close at midnight on Saturday under the Sunday law, Allen's saloon drew the largest crowd and closed its doors at 12:40 a.m. after a policeman's warning
Allen led a bloodied man who had refused to leave out of his saloon after a bouncer knocked him down
facts.quote: It don't pay to monkey with the talent.

notes: The crowd 'expected something to develop out of Tom's pugnacity', which may refer to the arrest in article 128 (May 19, 1888); not explained in the clipping. The saloon's address is not given here.
